- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to account for potential rebound.
- Model consistently overestimates in early periods of a 30-day forecast (especially days 1–5), especially after sharp price drops; apply downward bias of 3–8% for first 5 days.
- After a price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to lag behind true price; apply slight upward bias (1–3%) to catch mean reversion.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is trending upward but price is falling — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% to reflect sentiment divergence.
- In cases where true price drops sharply after a forecast peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days if sentiment is weak or negative.
